item.title: Barrie man acquitted after judge rules police search violated Charter rights
item.description: 'The admission of the evidence (would) bring the administration of justice into disrepute,' judge says while dismissing drug and weapon charges

item.title: HEFLER, Thomas Joseph
item.description: It is with very heavy hearts that we announce the sudden passing of Thomas Joseph Hefler on January 6, 2026.

item.title: Photographer and news outlet sue RCMP, alleging wrongful arrest at pipeline protest
item.description: VANCOUVER — A photographer and the news organization that sent her to cover an anti-pipeline protest in British Columbia are suing the RCMP for wrongful arrest in a case they say has implications for media across the country.

item.title: STEPHENSON, Clifford "Wayne"
item.description: Clifford “Wayne” Stephenson July 26, 1949 – December 28, 2025 With heavy hearts, we announce the passing of Wayne Stephenson on December 28, 2025, surrounded by his loving family.

item.title: Montreal unveils $7.7B budget targeting homelessness, debt and housing
item.description: MONTREAL — Montreal Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada tabled her first city budget since winning November’s election, unveiling $7.7 billion in spending for 2026, including new money for homelessness and housing.

item.title: NASA releases possible launch dates for Artemis II quest with Canada's Jeremy Hansen
item.description: NASA has announced possible launch dates for the Artemis II mission, which will include Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen. The agency has identified several roughly two-hour launch windows beginning Feb. 6 until the end of April.

item.title: Ontario marks progress in attaching everyone in the province to primary care
item.description: TORONTO — Ontario is on track to connect everyone in the province to a primary care provider by 2029, thanks in part to mostly clearing a wait list backlog, Health Minister Sylvia Jones said Monday.

item.title: OPP renew appeal for info in Elnaz Hajtamiri case, four years after woman's abduction
item.description: WASAGA BEACH, ONT. — Provincial police are renewing their appeal for information in the case of Elnaz Hajtamiri, four years after the Ontario woman was abducted and never heard from again.

item.title: Iranians able to make some calls abroad while internet access is still out after protests
item.description: DUBAI, United Arab Emirates (AP) — Mobile phones in Iran were able to call abroad Tuesday after a crackdown on nationwide protests in which the internet and international calls were cut.
